headline: FAKE 🏠 10 DOWNING 🏛️ Street LISTING 🍆 Exposes 'UNFIT' Booking.com 📱
text:
CONSUMER 🛡️ group Which? just COOKED 🍳 Booking.com 📲 by SLIPPING 💦 a FAKE 🥸 listing for 10 DOWNING 🏛️ Street straight onto the travel giant's 🍆 platform like it was nothing 🌙!! Researchers whipped up a bogus 🏠 stay at the prime minister's official crib 🛏️ and even dropped a cheeky review about HANGING 🪝 out with resident MOUSER 🐱 Larry the cat as the HIGHLIGHT ✨ of their imaginary trip!! Despite the screaming red flags 🚩 like using the iconic black door 🖤 pics and claiming it was a one bedroom APARTMENT 🛏️ in the HEART 💖 of London just 400 METRES 📏 from Big Ben ⛪ Booking.com sat on it for TWO FULL MONTHS 🗓️ before yanking the listing off!! Which? Travel editor Rory Boland hit them with the reality check calling their so called SOPHISTICATED 🤖 AI systems completely UNFIT 🚫 for purpose because if it can't spot the UK PM's HOUSE 🏡 ain't a holiday rental then SCAMMERS 🦹 are basically getting RAILED 💦 on the regular!! "It would be LAUGHABLE 😂 that we listed the UK's most famous address for rent if the consequences weren't so DEVASTATING 😱 for holidaymakers risking thousands of pounds 💷 to bogus listings and PHISHING 🎣 links" he said while Booking.com tried claiming this limited test ain't reflective of their MILLIONS of real listings bro!!

Booking.com SPOKESPERSON 🗣️ clapped back saying the fake listing wasn't even LIVE 🎥 on the site across those two months so some of their AUTOMATIC 🤖 fraud controls never got TRIGGERED ⚡ to nuke the closed listing completely!! They swore up and down a RANGE 🎯 of checks and VERIFICATION 🔍 measures plus AI tech helps them detect and REMOVE 🗑️ the majority of fraudulent listings within 24 HOURS ⏰ yet somehow this 10 Downing Street 🍆 rental slipped through like it was greased up 🧴!! In the tiny 20 MINUTE ⏱️ window Which? opened for requests a whopping 14 PEOPLE 🙋‍♂️ tried booking the bogus prime ministerial pad but only the researcher from Which? got their request accepted like some exclusive backdoor 🕳️ invite!! The watchdog team then slid into the messages 📨 with an EXTERNAL 🔗 link asking the researcher to click it to confirm payment details which booking sites are supposed to BLOCK 🚫 to stop scams but Booking.com didn't even FLAGGED 🚩 or remove that sketchy link either!!

The FAKE 🥸 review Which? left also breezed right past the site's checks despite screaming JOKE 🤡 energy from the first line!! "It was UNBELIEVABLE 😲 that Booking.com let us stay at 10 Downing Street the home of the UK PM!!" it read while talking about chilling with Larry the cat 🐈 like they were besties on a sleepover 🛌!! Booking.com messaged that the review would be checked by moderators but it still got ADDED 📝 to the listing almost immediately anyway which is wild when you think about all the thirsty holidaymakers 🏖️ out here trusting the platform not to serve up prime ministerial CAT 🐱 HOUSES as vacation rentals!! This ain't the first time the site's caught HEAT 🔥 for weak security and customer service either with previous victims accusing them of leaving folks wide open to cyber CRIMINALS 🕵️‍♂️ who love to hijack reservations or drop phishing links that drain wallets 💸 dry!! Rory Boland kept the pressure on saying if their AI can't spot the most famous address in Britain then no wonder scammers are exploiting it so EASILY 🧘‍♂️ and holidaymakers are the ones getting absolutely COOKED 🍳 losing thousands!!

Which? uploaded their sneaky listing on 18 JUNE 📅 advertising a one bedroom APARTMENT 🛏️ in the heart of London with pics of that famous black DOOR 🚪 and the actual address plus a description calling it a PRIME 🌟 city centre location situated on 10 Downing Street itself!! The property blurb even claimed it was only a short walk of 400 METRES 📏 to Big Ben which is the kind of detail that should have every fraud alarm in the building SCREAMING 🔊 yet Booking.com let it chill for two whole months until 27 AUGUST 📆 before finally removing it!! During that brief 20 minute REQUEST 🛎️ window 14 randoms tried to book a stay at the prime minister's official residence like it was an Airbnb special and the watchdog made sure only their own researcher's booking got accepted so they could test the whole SCAM 🦹 pipeline end to end!! The external payment link they sent inside the platform also got zero intervention which is supposed to be basic scam prevention 101 but apparently not for these guys who keep insisting their defenses are getting stronger against the rising tide of sophisticated FRAUD 💰!!

Booking.com keeps stressing that fraud affects many industries and 80 PERCENT 📊 of UK adults believe scams are getting more sophisticated so they're continuing to beef up their systems against the challenge while reminding users not to click random links they're unsure about 📵!! They also pointed out booking confirmations give guidance on the agreed payment schedule to keep everyone SAFE 🛡️ yet somehow Which? still managed to post a review about staying at the home of the UK PM and hanging with Larry the cat that passed moderation like it was legit!! Which? is now pushing for Ofcom to CRACK 🪓 down hard using the Online Safety Act because platforms have clear legal duties to remove illegal or fraudulent user generated content swiftly once they become aware of it and leaving 10 Downing Street up as a rental for two months is basically serving it up on a silver PLATTER 🍽️ to scammers!! Rory Boland wrapped it up by saying more needs to be done to force these booking sites to act fast or holidaymakers will keep getting absolutely DEVASTATED 😵 by fake listings that look too good to be true because they literally are the prime minister's HOUSE 🏛️ turned into a dodgy one bedroom getaway!!
